No. 105481
Date 21/3/17

March 21,

Sir Everard D.H. Fraser, K.C.M.G.,
H.B.M's Consul-General,
Shanghai.

Confidential.

My dear Sir Everard,

Between 2.15 and 3.30 p.m. March
20, a meeting was held in the Chinese Y.M.C.A.
building, Szechuen Road. About 400 students of the
German Medical and Engineering School were present.
Tang Shao Yi (唐紹儀), Wei Siao Foo (魏少甫),
manager of the Venus Insurance Co., the manager of
a Tobacco Company on Nanking Road, and several Chinese
teachers of the German School attended. Mr. Wei Siao
Foo told the students that the above mentioned Insur-
ance and the Tobacco Company had arranged with the Foh
Lee Kung (福利公), Ta Yuen (致遠), Tsung Teh (振泰)
and Kai Tah (開泰) Hotels to provide the students
with lodging, and that if any of them were in financial
difficulties, they might call at room No. 41 of the
first named hotel and receive assistance. He added
that those who were living with their relatives and
friends should remain with them. He also said that
the Committee of the Venus Insurance Company and that
of the Chung Hwa Book Store had wired to the Minister
of Education asking him to make arrangements with the
Foreign Ministers to enable the scholars to continue
their studies.

Tang Shao Yi said that the Paulun Hospital could
not accomodate so many students and that Liang Chi
Chao (梁啟超) should be asked as to whether he would

3月21日，

Everard D.H. Fraser 爵士，K.C.M.G.，
英国驻上海总领事，
上海。

机密。

亲爱的 Everard 爵士：

3月20日下午2时15分至3时30分之间，在四川路中华基督教青年会大楼举行了一次会议。约有400名德国医学与工程学校的学生出席。唐绍仪、金星保险公司经理魏少甫（Wei Siao Foo）、南京路一家烟草公司经理以及德国学校的几位中国教师参加了会议。魏少甫先生告诉学生，上述保险公司和烟草公司已与福利公、致远、振泰和开泰旅馆安排妥当，为学生提供住宿；如果任何学生遇到经济困难，可前往第一家提到的旅馆的41号房间寻求援助。他补充说，那些与亲友同住的学生应继续与他们住在一起。他还表示，金星保险公司委员会和中华书局委员会已致电教育总长，请他与各国公使进行安排，以便学生们能够继续学业。

唐绍仪表示，宝隆医院无法容纳如此多的学生，并建议询问梁启超是否愿意

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
POLICE FORCE,
(DETECTIVE BRANCH)
Shanghai Municipal Council.
21st March 1917.

Sir,
Between 2.15 and 3.30 p.m. 20th inst a meeting was held in the Chinese Y.M.C.A. building, Szechuen Road. About 400 students of the German Medical and Engineering School were present. Tang Shao Yi, 唐紹儀 Wei Siao Foo 魏小甫, manager of the Venus Insurance Co, the manager of a Tobacco Company on Nanking Road, and several Chinese teachers of the German school attended. Mr. Wei Siao Foo told the students that the above mentioned Insurance and the Tobacco Company had arranged with the Poh Lee Kung 福利公, Ts Yuen, 致遠 Tsung Tah 振泰 and Kai Tah 開泰 Hotels to provide the students with lodging, and that if any of them were financial difficulties, they might call at room No. 41 of the first named hotel and receive assistance. He added that those who were living with their relatives and friends should remain with them. He also said that the Committee of the Venus Insurance Company and that of the ChungHua Book Store had wired to the Minister of Education, asking him to make arrangements with the Foreign Ministers to enable the scholars to continue their studies.
Tang Shao Yi said that the Paulun Hospital could not accomodate so many students and that Liang Chi Chao 梁啟超 should be asked as to whether he would allow the students to use the premises of the Chinese College at Woosung which were now vacant. Should Liang refuse, another suitable place would be chosen. One of the Chinese teachers suggested that he should go and interview Chu Pao San 朱葆三 and Pae Jen Sun 貝潤生, asking them to wire to Liang Chi Chao, conveying the above request.
Nothing was said about political situation. The German teachers are said to be willing to continue the instructions as soon as the Chinese students are in a position to resume their work.

AH
21/3

Your obedient servant,
mmmmmustura
Chief Detective Inspector.

Captain Superintendent of Police.

occupying 6 rooms.

Your obedient servant
A. Ruth

POLICE FORCE,
(DETECTIVE BRANCH.)

March 19th 1917

Sir,
The premises of the German Medical and Engineering
School in the French Concession were occupied by the
French Police on Saturday March 18th.
The Principal was called to the French Police
Station and informed of the steps which were going
to be taken. He made no demur and entered into
a discussion as to arrangements to dispose of the
students. Those of the latter who belong to
this locality and those who have friends here left
at once whilst those whose homes are some distance
off are remaining in the school until they can
communicate with their relatives.
Thirteen are at present in lodging house at
No.57 Fohkien Road, nineteen at No.56 Shantung Road,
five in 33 Avenue Edward VII, one in 689 Canton Road
and four 229 Honan Road.
They seem to be quite unconcerned over the matter
and do not at all appear to be harbouring any
feelings of resentment over their eviction.

Your Obedient Servant,

William Musting
Chief Detective Inspector.

Captain Superintendent of Police.

ASH
19/3

March 20th    1917

REPORT ON Paying off coolies from the German Medical
School, Frenchtown.

Made by D. A. Sullivan.    Forwarded by Chief Detective Inspector.

Sir
I respectfully beg to report that between 3 p.m.
and 5 p.m. 19th inst. about forty workmen, comprising
carpenters, fitters, brass-smiths, and coolies, formerly
employed at the German Medical College, Avenue Du
Roi Albert, Frenchtown, were paid off at 3 Sicawei Rd
Two Germans from the school brought the money
and paid the men.
I talked to the coolies, who told me they had been
dismissed indefinitely and were now looking for other
employment.
3 Sicawei Rd is a garden and stable used by
Mr Rosenbaum and Mr Tiefenbacher, and I believe
there is a man named Hohenfelde living there.

I beg to remain
Sir
Your Obedient Servant
J. Sullivan, Det Sergt

The Chief Detective Inspector.

have to leave.

Confidential.

Capt.
Per yr. inform: These pupils
who are mostly Germans are likely
to swell the ranks of the
agitations; but I have
instructed Cpl. to keep close in touch
with them as no doubt the French authorities
will - I think it would be wise to pass on this
Captain Superintendent of Police.

is no news of the German Minister.

Noted
